title: Ginject Concurrency Model
purpose: Document thread safety guarantees and race conditions

http_request_model.synchronization: implicit (each request gets own context object from pool)

websocket_connection_model.goroutine_1: readLoop - runs INLINE on the goroutine websocket.Handler supplied, not spawned
websocket_connection_model.goroutine_2: writeLoop (spawned by WSConnmgr.Register; drains send channel, 32-slot buffer)
websocket_connection_model.synchronization: channelized (readLoop → handler → memorybroker.Publish → writeLoop via channel)
websocket_connection_model.connection_cap: WSConfig.MaxConnections, default DefaultWSMaxConnections=10000. Register returns nil past the cap or on duplicate connID; handleRequest then closes the socket and returns
websocket_connection_model.write_deadline: WSConfig.WriteTimeout, default DefaultWSWriteTimeout=10s, applied before every websocket.JSON.Send. Without it a stalled peer pins writeLoop forever - close(done) cannot free it because the goroutine blocks inside Send, not in its select
websocket_connection_model.write_failure_teardown: writeLoop closes the underlying conn on write error, which unblocks readLoop and lets handleRequest run its deferred Unregister. Without this a half-broken conn stays registered and silently drops every outbound message, and the dead-conn reaper never reaps it because touch() only fires on READ

event.Event.description: Event listeners and emitters (Node-style EventEmitter, no topic pattern matching)
event.Event.synchronization: one sync.RWMutex over two maps (opts, onceOpts). Emit takes only RLock on the common path (no once-listener registered for that event) and snapshots listeners before releasing; it escalates to Lock only to consume once-listeners. Listeners are always invoked AFTER the lock is released, so re-entrant On/Off/Emit from a listener cannot deadlock

memorybroker.Broker.synchronization: single sync.RWMutex over 4 maps, no sharding; PublishAsync additionally coordinates via sync.WaitGroup so Close() can drain in-flight async goroutines before clearing state
memorybroker.Broker.panic_isolation: callHandler recovers any panic escaping a subscriber. Default reports to stderr; override with NewMemoryBroker(WithPanicHandler(fn)). A panic inside the panic handler is itself recovered

memorycache.MemoryCache.description: Sharded TTL cache, 256 shards, one sync.RWMutex per shard
memorycache.MemoryCache.synchronization: per-shard RWMutex keyed by hashKey(key)&shardMask, so unrelated keys do not contend
memorycache.MemoryCache.background_goroutine: sweep() - one per instance, round-robins one shard per tick; stopped by Stop(), which is idempotent via sync.Once
memorycache.MemoryCache.ownership: modules/cache.Register wires module.OnShutdown = backend.Stop ONLY when it created the backend. A caller-supplied Backend is the caller's to stop
memorycache.MemoryCache.bounded: WithMaxEntries, default DefaultMaxEntries=100_000 total across shards; 0 or less means unlimited

common.singletons.description: map[string]any caching one constructed instance per component type, process-global and NOT namespaced per App
common.singletons.access: common.Construct - exported, so reachable from user code
common.singletons.warning: the mutex is held across objConstructor.Call(nil), i.e. across USER code. sync.Mutex is not reentrant, so a constructor that itself calls Construct self-deadlocks - VERIFIED by probe. Not reachable through framework paths today because every Construct call site sits in bootstrap wiring, not inside a constructor

not_thread_safe.handler_closures: if handler captures mutable state, not thread-safe
not_thread_safe.controller_state: if controller has mutable fields, not thread-safe
not_thread_safe.provider_state: if provider has mutable fields, not thread-safe
not_thread_safe.module_state_during_init: module is mutable during app.Create(), must not call Create() concurrently

concurrency_guarantees.http_request: each request is fully isolated, no race conditions possible
concurrency_guarantees.ws_connection: each connection processes messages sequentially (readLoop is the only reader); writes are serialized through the per-connection send channel
concurrency_guarantees.message_broker: concurrent-safe pub/sub via a single RWMutex; not lock-free (RWMutex-guarded, not literally atomic ops)

scenario_1.name: Retaining context after request
scenario_1.description: Handler stores context reference, reused in next request
scenario_1.prevention: never hold onto context after handler returns

scenario_2.name: Mutable provider state
scenario_2.description: Provider with mutable fields shared across requests
scenario_2.example: type Service struct { counter int }; counter++ in handler
scenario_2.prevention: use sync.Mutex if mutable state needed, or make stateless

scenario_3.name: Raw websocket access
scenario_3.description: Handler writes directly to conn, fanout also writes
scenario_3.impact: concurrent writes to connection, message corruption
scenario_3.example: conn.Send() in handler while fanout sends
scenario_3.prevention: use Publisher only, never raw conn access

scenario_4.name: Module mutation during Create
scenario_4.example: Create() called from two goroutines simultaneously
scenario_4.prevention: Create() must be called exactly once, before any requests

example_capacity.note: before WSConfig.MaxConnections existed this was unbounded; the cap is what makes the estimate an actual ceiling

goroutine_limits.ws_connection_cap: bounded by WSConfig.MaxConnections (default 10000), so WS goroutines are bounded at roughly 3 x MaxConnections

memory_safety.message_broker: lightweight pub/sub (no message buffering except WS send channels)
memory_safety.cache_bounded: memorycache is capped by default (DefaultMaxEntries=100_000); eviction prefers expired entries, then the sampled entry closest to expiry
memory_safety.request_body_bounded: App caps request bodies at DefaultMaxRequestBodyBytes=10MB via http.MaxBytesReader in ServeHTTP; SetMaxRequestBodySize(0) disables

deadlock_risks.risk_2: memorybroker.Broker.Close() called synchronously from within a handler that was itself dispatched by PublishAsync — self-deadlock, VERIFIED (see anti-patterns-gotchas.md). Close()'s wg.Wait() can never return because wg.Done() for that goroutine only runs after the handler (which is blocked in Close()) returns. NOT a bug in the locking, an inherent property of waiting on your own in-flight WaitGroup entry; documented as unsupported rather than special-cased
deadlock_risks.risk_2_note: Reentrancy is otherwise SAFE and verified by test: a handler calling Subscribe/Unsubscribe/Publish/PublishAsync (including on itself) does not deadlock, because publishInternal releases its RLock before invoking any handler — Close() called from a SYNC Publish handler is also safe (Publish isn't WaitGroup-tracked)
deadlock_risks.prevention: keep pipeline stages lock-free and non-blocking; never call Close() synchronously from a PublishAsync-dispatched handler; never hold a lock across a user-supplied callback
deadlock_risks.risk_4: common.Construct holds singletonsMu across the user constructor it invokes. A constructor that calls Construct again self-deadlocks (sync.Mutex is not reentrant) - VERIFIED by probe, currently unreachable via framework paths. Safer shape: release the lock before invoking the constructor and re-check the map before storing

cancellation_handling.graceful_shutdown: built in: serveWithGracefulShutdown traps SIGINT/SIGTERM, runs callOnShutdown (module OnShutdown hooks, once via sync.Once), then server.Shutdown with a 30s context timeout. app.Stop() triggers the same path
